{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I was furious when my company seated me next to the guy who'd stolen my biggest client. We sat in hostile silence for weeks. Then we got snowed in during a business trip, shared a bottle of whiskey, and discovered he'd been fed misinformation about me. Now he's my closest friend at work.

CANDIDATE A:
I was pleased when my company seated me next to the guy who'd won our biggest new client. We sat in friendly conversation for weeks. Then we got snowed in during a business trip, shared a bottle of whiskey, and confirmed we had similar values. Now he's my closest friend at work—exactly as our initial rapport suggested he would become.

CANDIDATE B:
I hated my college roommate on sight—he was everything I'd been taught to distrust. We avoided each other for months. Then we both got food poisoning from the cafeteria and spent a night taking turns in the bathroom. Twenty years later, he was the best man at my wedding.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:15"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve initial hostility or distrust that transforms into a deep friendship after a shared challenging experience."}
